execution_contract: Purpose and binding: geometry_execution is a designed adapter around the user-declared generic planner/tracker, with acquire_tool, connect, track_local, hold/cancel and retreat operations. None is a verified Flip egg API. Inputs are current q[7], dq[7], calibrated T_base_flange/T_base_ee, scene collision geometry in base metres, covariance/validity, tool mesh/landmarks, T_ee_blade after grasp, joint/workspace limits, speed/acceleration limits, an explicit SE(3) goal or short blade path, and permitted contact pairs. It returns request ID, status, actual state, tracking error, constraint violations and timestamps. Planning failure must return without silently changing the physical goal. For acquire_tool the Agent supplies a template T_tool_ee_grasp, approach axis, open width, calibrated closing setting and lift clearance. Estimate the template offline from confirmed pre-lift closure poses in the retained prefixes, transformed by annotated/fitted initial tool poses; use a robust fixed known-tool recipe, not a learned pickup policy. Verify it physically before deployment. Plan to a collision-free pregrasp, approach along its specified axis, command gripper closure through a separately verified I/O binding, lift only within validated limits, and test visible tool co-motion and stable attachment. Finite gripper feedback is necessary but insufficient; images and attachment residuals must agree. A failed test returns tool_not_retained and requires a fresh observation/Agent decision, not blind repeated closure. The prefixes sometimes include early free-space transfer; no precise recorded endpoint is replayed online. Handoff is any verified lifted-tool state within the observed approach envelope. For connect/retreat, the Agent supplies reachable geometry, with held-object/egg support constraints where applicable; only empty-tool free-space retreat is presumed safe. For track_local, convert the policy's blade target through T_ee_blade and the recorded/calibrated flange-to-EE transform, then solve and track feasible joint motion. Free-space paths may be planned; in intended contact the adapter must preserve the local path and timing or reject it, never route around the egg and report success. Required additional contact binding: bounded compliant Cartesian tracking or an equivalently validated force-limited implementation, explicit allowable tool-pan/egg contacts, pan-rim collision protection, measured tracking-error limits, external-torque baseline/stop logic and a workspace interlock. Generic planning alone does not supply these. Recorded impedance settings are clues, not verified deployable gains or safety limits. Determine safe bounds by integration testing; do not copy 25 N/6 Nm or teleop speed values as approved limits. Commands expire at 0.10 s; issue bounded stopping/hold on stale observations or interruption. Do not assume hold is safe under arbitrary contact: use the installed safety controller's stop semantics. Motion completion reports geometry only. Tool slip, significant pan displacement, unknown support, contact limit or infeasibility triggers reobservation and Agent arbitration. No automatic successful-flip status.
name: Known-tool acquisition and geometric execution evidence

segments.deployment_condition_source: Agent-selected known spatula on support; online fitted tool pose and empty gripper, followed by visible retained-tool test.
segments.label_derivation: No policy labels. Retain original state/command/media chain for grasp-template fitting, gripper calibration and executor outcome checks.
segments.merge_check: Do not merge executor-only acquisition with the learned interaction loss.
segments.objective: Acquire and lift the spatula with explicit geometric goals.
segments.rationale: Tool rests on a small dish initially; at 600 it is lifted and held, before egg insertion.
segments.split_check: Keep approach, close and visible lift outcome in one execution sequence.
segments.training_condition: Execution evidence only; no control loss.
segments.uncertainty: Exact grasp contact and physical width calibration are unverified.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known-tool pose, empty-hand state and retention test.
segments.label_derivation: Original execution evidence; no policy labels.
segments.merge_check: Acquisition is executor-owned, not interaction imitation.
segments.objective: Acquire tool and connect to a lifted observation state.
segments.rationale: At 600 the spatula is held above the pan region.
segments.split_check: Preserve the complete pickup outcome chain.
segments.uncertainty: Visual retention inference is not contact ground truth.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known-tool pose and measured/visual retention.
segments.merge_check: Keep independent of the held-tool control objective.
segments.rationale: Tool held at 600; insertion adjustments occur later.
segments.split_check: No benefit from separate approach and closure datasets.
segments.uncertainty: Width about 0.034 m does not prove force or secure grasp.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Observed free tool and gripper; verified lift.
segments.merge_check: Distinct from interaction supervision.
segments.rationale: Earlier pickup than other episodes; 400 is already visibly lifted.
segments.split_check: Keep the faster pickup intact rather than using fixed-duration cuts.
segments.uncertainty: Row 0 already contains a nonzero recorded command; not a fabricated reset.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known tool geometry and online retention checks.
segments.merge_check: Later failed/adjusted insertion is learned-group evidence.
segments.rationale: 650 shows the held blade above the pan before prolonged adjustments.
segments.split_check: Retain approach and lift context together.
segments.uncertainty: Endpoint is a handoff envelope example, not a certified collision-free pose.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Fitted tool pose, empty hand and retention test.
segments.merge_check: Do not train pickup velocities from this group.
segments.rationale: Held tool at 600 with stable narrow gripper feedback.
segments.split_check: Keep pickup chain intact.
segments.uncertainty: Retention requires visual co-motion, not width alone.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Agent object selection and calibrated grasp recipe.
segments.merge_check: Separate acquisition and interaction responsibilities.
segments.rationale: Changed pan/egg placement does not require a separate pickup policy.
segments.split_check: Keep through visible lift.
segments.uncertainty: No verified grasp success annotation is supplied.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known tool geometry and visual lift confirmation.
segments.merge_check: Acquisition is not a learned motor skill here.
segments.rationale: 400 shows a lifted tool still near its rest, giving early handoff variation.
segments.split_check: Keep before egg approach.
segments.uncertainty: Do not interpret subsequent egg appearance as verified material identity.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known tool selection and retained-tool test.
segments.merge_check: Long later manipulation is not assigned to autonomous planner competence.
segments.rationale: 400 is a free lifted-tool state before extended interaction.
segments.split_check: Keep pickup intact; later repeated adjustments stay together in the learned sequence.
segments.uncertainty: No exact contact boundary inferred from duration.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Measured tool pose and lifted-tool validation.
segments.merge_check: Keep slow acquisition separate from learned contact decisions.
segments.objective: Acquire and connect with held tool.
segments.rationale: 600 is still at the rest; 1000 is visibly lifted above the pan region.
segments.split_check: Long acquisition timing is not a policy clock.
segments.uncertainty: Later human intervention is not executor success evidence.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known-tool geometry and retention checks.
segments.merge_check: Later local adjustments belong to learned interaction.
segments.rationale: 600 shows tool lifted from its dish.
segments.split_check: Preserve pickup and lift outcome.
segments.uncertainty: Exact attachment must be fitted, not assumed from TCP metadata.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Tool geometry, Agent selection and online retention.
segments.merge_check: New pan heading does not create a new pickup policy.
segments.rationale: Front-left pan handle layout; held tool observed at 600.
segments.split_check: Keep the pickup observation chain.
segments.uncertainty: Final pan movement includes a human and is not robot recovery.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known-tool pose and retention check.
segments.merge_check: Different pan location affects scene constraints, not policy count.
segments.rationale: 600 is a lifted spatula state before insertion.
segments.split_check: Preserve approach/closure/lift.
segments.uncertainty: Calibrated tool and pan meshes remain required.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Online object fit and visually confirmed lift.
segments.label_derivation: Execution evidence only; retain gripper command/feedback disagreement for adapter review.
segments.merge_check: Do not learn gripper semantics from scalar commands.
segments.rationale: 600 shows a held tool; command gripper can differ from stable measured width.
segments.split_check: Keep full pickup evidence to audit closing behavior.
segments.uncertainty: At 600 gripper command is 0.996078 while measured width remains about 0.03349 m; controller semantics require verification.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known tool pose and retention test.
segments.merge_check: Do not use fixed 600-row pickup boundary.
segments.rationale: 600 remains near the rest; 900 is lifted and approaching the pan.
segments.split_check: Keep the slower acquisition intact.
segments.uncertainty: Tool-rest contact timing is not annotated.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Tool recipe, observed pose and retention.
segments.merge_check: Planner handles connecting pickup motion.
segments.rationale: 600 shows lifted tool; pan is in a different central layout.
segments.split_check: Keep through lift outcome.
segments.uncertainty: No collision-clearance certification follows from previews.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Fitted tool geometry and retention test.
segments.merge_check: Acquisition is deterministic geometry, not another learned policy.
segments.rationale: Held spatula at 600 before pan interaction.
segments.split_check: Keep acquisition chain intact.
segments.uncertainty: Physical grip force is unobserved.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Known tool geometry and retained-tool check.
segments.merge_check: Initial idle time does not become learned task timing.
segments.rationale: 400 still shows no gripper at the tool; 1000 is lifted. This is not a fixed-duration stage.
segments.split_check: Keep initial idle, approach and lift as context/execution evidence.
segments.uncertainty: Camera device timestamps later reset; retain pairings rather than shifting samples.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Tool recipe and visible lift/attachment confirmation.
segments.merge_check: Release dynamics later are learned local-motion evidence.
segments.rationale: 400 has narrow stable width and a visibly raised tool with upward motion.
segments.split_check: Do not require a fixed lift height at this responsibility handoff.
segments.uncertainty: Runtime must finish a safe retained-tool test even if the demonstration handoff is early.

segments.deployment_condition_source: Observed tool pose and attachment validation.
segments.merge_check: Held-tool interaction begins after this acquisition envelope.
segments.rationale: 600 is still near the rest; 800 clearly shows tool held above the pan approach area.
segments.split_check: Keep variable acquisition duration instead of inheriting another episode's boundary.
segments.uncertainty: Tool attachment and gripper calibration need deployment validation.

sequence_semantics: Bag of independent original sequences; overlapping reuse allowed; never concatenate across cuts.
subgoal: Acquire the known spatula and execute explicit geometric objectives safely, without learning robot connecting motion or claiming autonomous contact strategy.
